Question: Let \(\clubsuit(x)\) denote the sum of the digits of the positive integer \(x.\) For example, \(\clubsuit(8)=8\) and \(\clubsuit(123)=1+2+3=6.\) For how many two-digit values of \(x\) is \(\clubsuit(\clubsuit(x))=3?\)
Solution:
First determine what the inner digit sum can be. Let \(a\) and \(b\) be the tens and units digits of \(x\), so \(1\le a\le9\) and \(0\le b\le9\). Then
\[
s=\clubsuit(x)=a+b
\]
is an integer from \(1\) through \(18\).

Among these possible values of \(s\), the only ones with digit sum \(3\) are \(3\) and \(12\). Indeed, a single-digit value must itself be \(3\); a two-digit value in this range has tens digit \(1\), so its units digit must be \(2\).

If \(a+b=3\), the possible numbers are \(12,21,30\), giving \(3\) numbers.

If \(a+b=12\), the tens digit can be any integer from \(3\) through \(9\), and the units digit is then fixed as \(12-a\). This gives \(39,48,57,66,75,84,93\), or \(7\) numbers.

These cases exhaust the possible first digit sums and cannot overlap. Therefore the count is
\[
3+7=\boxed{10},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
